subject: Cardio Logic — request for senior override on Hosted API pricing
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cardiologic.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@cardiologic.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@procurepartners.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API pricing — ask for exceptional commercial terms

Sean — really appreciate the demo yesterday. We ran the numbers and expect sustained monthly token consumption well north of 10B tokens starting Q4 with a multi-year ramp. That profile is transformative for us but requires >20% off your standard Hosted API list to make the economics work across our payer integrations.

Request: senior approval for a 25% off-hosted-usage rate (or equivalent committed-rate model) tied to a 24-month minimum and quarterly usage gates. We can accelerate a PO and legal review if finance has clarity on discounted tiers.

Attached: projected usage sheet and a first-pass SOW. Happy to jump on a call this afternoon.

—Jordan
VP Product, CardioLogic
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cardiologic.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — ask for exceptional commercial terms

Jordan — thanks for the clear numbers and for sending the SOW. I’m looping in Ben (deal desk) and Neha (sales lead) to expedite review. Quick summary of what CardioLogic is asking for: 25% off Hosted API list, conditioned on a 24-month minimum and aggressive usage gates.

Internal ask: Ben/Neha — can we approve anything above 20% here? If not, what approval path/exec signoff is required and what commercial levers (commit length, minimum spend, SKU mix, termination penalties) would make a 22–25% concession acceptable?

Next steps from our side: Ben, can you run margin sensitivity and propose a recommended counter we can present to Jordan by EOD? I’ll stand by for the DocuSign/SOW updates.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — ask for exceptional commercial terms

Team — reviewed Jordan’s attachments. Highlights:
- Baseline annualized consumption (year 1) — ~120B tokens; year 2 ramps toward 250B+.
- 25% off list would drop unit economics below break-even on current pricing for non-quantized, streaming-heavy traffic unless we secure aggressive caching/quantization/infra credits.

Recommended commercial posture:
1) Offer a conditional 22% usage discount (hosted price) in exchange for: 24-month commitment, quarterly minimums equal to 60% of projected ramp, and a quarterly review clause tied to latency/SLO adherence.
2) Add a technical optimization clause: Redwood will provide model/quantization recommendations and up to 3 weeks of implementation support to recover margin.
3) Include an early-exit clawback if usage drops >35% vs. committed quarterly minimum for two consecutive quarters.

This requires senior approval (Finance + Head of Sales) because it reduces hosted gross margins materially. Mina — requesting exec signoff on a 22% exception (not to exceed) with the commercial guardrails above. If Mina approves, legal will need the SOW updated with the minimums and clawback language (I’ve attached a redline checklist).

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (sensitivity), suggested_sla_clawback_notes.docx (stub).

—Ben
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — ask for exceptional commercial terms

Ben/Sean/Neha — I reviewed Ben’s sensitivity and CardioLogic’s projected ramp. Given strategic value (large national payer integrations + reference customer potential) I’m willing to approve an exception up to 22% off Hosted API usage under these strict conditions:

- 24-month firm commitment with monthly invoicing and a 60% first-quarter minimum (committed tokens).
- Quarterly true-up and a clawback mechanism: credits applied if usage falls below 65% of committed quarterly tokens for two consecutive quarters.
- Redwood retains right to suspend promotional pricing if SLOs (latency >200ms 95th for streaming) are not met for two sequential months.
- Legal to add an implementation milestone tied to our optimization support (3 weeks) and a performance acceptance sign-off.

I am not comfortable with 25% at this stage. Approving 22% contingent upon the above mitigations. Legal and Finance to finalize language; procurement to confirm PO/AR details before DocuSign.

Mina Haddad
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@cardiologic.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@cardiologic.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — ask for exceptional commercial terms

Jordan — good news. Leadership has approved a commercial exception: 22% off Hosted API usage, conditioned on the guardrails Ben and Mina outlined (24-month commitment, quarterly minimums, implementation support and clawback language).

Next steps:
1) I’ll share an updated SOW and pricing appendix with the exact quarterly minimums and clawback wording by EOD tomorrow.
2) Legal will prepare the DocuSign package; procurement, please confirm the PO cadence and billing contact.
3) Ben and our Solutions team will schedule the 3-week optimization block post-signature.

Attachments: CardioLogic_SOW_v1.2.pdf (SOW draft), CardioLogic_ProjectedUsage_2028-2030.xlsx (for reference).

Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the gates and the implementation plan.

—Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
